children: Cattle slaughter fell to a non-holiday record low last week, at 484,000 head, says AgResource in a note. This supported higher cut-out prices for cattle, but that doesn't seem to be enough to give cattle a boost in early trade. Cattle instead appears to be locked in the negative momentum seen across commodities, including grain futures. Livestock traders are looking for some sort of sign of cattle beginning a prolonged rebound. "Last week's chart gaps likely need to be closed before a meaningful recovery can get underway," says AgResource. Live cattle falls 0.1%, and lean hogs drop 0.6%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
